correctness.rationale: Exact box-containment follows from coordinatewise corner extrema. Squaring half-widths turns volume optimization into a strictly concave log-product problem on three pair-sum inequalities. Verified positive KKT multipliers in the three-active branch and first-two-active branch give global optimality; strict concavity gives the unique half-widths. Two active equalities enforce unique centering. Explicit witness proves the third cylinder changes the body until \(\gamma=\alpha+\beta\), although the box freezes at smaller \(\gamma_*\). Direct differentiation gives the \(C^1\)-but-not-\(C^2\) log-volume boundary. The extracted standard-library checker passed 2,507 triples and 80 feasible competitors each; 250 independent SciPy optimization tests agreed to \(1.23\times10^{-6}\) relative error. Computations support but do not establish universality.

value.rationale: A complete sharp classification of optimal axis-aligned cuboid packing in a natural 3-cylinder Steinmetz family answers which constraints actually control a practical convex-body box approximation. The transition strictly precedes geometric redundancy, producing a provable interval where changing the solid leaves its unique packed cuboid invariant. The C1 but non-C2 optimal-volume response identifies a meaningful sensitivity boundary; neither effect follows from simply reporting the equal-radius tricylinder volume.
